# Esther Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 456v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** After these things, when the anger of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.

**2:2** Then the king's attendants who served him said, "Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.

**2:3** Let the king appoint commissioners in all the provinces of his kingdom to gather every beautiful young virgin to the citadel of Susa, to the house of the women, under the care of Hegai, the king's eunuch and guardian of the women. Let their beauty treatments be given to them.

**2:4** Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in place of Vashti." The matter pleased the king, and he did so.

**2:5** Now there was in the citadel of Susa a Jewish man named Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjaminite,

**2:6** who had been carried away from Jerusalem among the captives exiled with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile.

**2:7** He was the guardian of Hadassah — that is, Esther — his uncle's daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was beautiful in form and lovely in appearance, and when her father and mother died, Mordecai adopted her as his own daughter.

**2:8** When the king's order and decree were proclaimed, and many young women were gathered to the citadel of Susa under the care of Hegai, Esther also was taken to the king's palace and placed in the custody of Hegai, guardian of the women.

**2:9** The young woman pleased him and won his favor. He quickly provided her with beauty treatments and her portion of food, along with seven chosen attendants from the king's palace, and he transferred her and her attendants to the best quarters in the house of the women.

**2:10** Esther had not revealed her people or her ancestry, for Mordecai had instructed her not to make it known.

**2:11** Every day Mordecai walked back and forth near the courtyard of the house of the women, to learn how Esther was faring and what was happening to her.

**2:12** Each young woman's turn came to go in to King Ahasuerus after she had completed twelve months of preparation according to the regulations for the women — six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and cosmetics.

**2:13** When the young woman went in to the king, she was given whatever she requested to take with her from the house of the women to the king's palace.

**2:14** She would go in during the evening and return in the morning to a second house of the women, under the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch and guardian of the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless the king took delight in her and she was summoned by name.

**2:15** When the turn came for Esther — the daughter of Abihail, uncle of Mordecai, who had adopted her as his daughter — to go in to the king, she asked for nothing beyond what Hegai, the king's eunuch and guardian of the women, advised. And Esther found favor in the eyes of all who saw her.

**2:16** Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in the tenth month, the month of Tevet, in the seventh year of his reign.

**2:17** The king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she won more favor and devotion from him than all the other virgins. He set the royal crown upon her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.

**2:18** Then the king gave a great banquet in Esther's honor for all his officials and servants. He proclaimed a remission of taxes for the provinces and distributed gifts with royal generosity.

**2:19** When the virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.

**2:20** Esther still had not revealed her ancestry or her people, just as Mordecai had instructed her, for Esther continued to follow Mordecai's guidance as she had done when she was under his care.

**2:21** In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, who guarded the threshold, became angry and conspired to assassinate King Ahasuerus.

**2:22** The plot became known to Mordecai, and he reported it to Queen Esther, who informed the king in Mordecai's name.

**2:23** When the matter was investigated and found to be true, the two conspirators were hanged on a pole. And this was recorded in the Book of the Chronicles in the presence of the king.

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **"Won his favor" (2:9, 2:17):** The Hebrew uses the phrase *nassa chesed*, literally "she lifted up covenant-faithfulness." The word *chesed* carries deep covenantal meaning throughout the Hebrew Bible. In Esther, its use without any explicit divine reference is striking — suggesting that covenantal favor operates even in a seemingly secular setting.

2. **"Hanged on a pole" (2:23):** The Hebrew *al etz* means literally "on a tree" or "on wood." Persian execution typically involved impalement on a stake, not hanging by a rope. LOGOS renders this as "hanged on a pole" to avoid the modern association of "hanging" while remaining close to the Hebrew construction.

3. **Mordecai at the king's gate (2:19, 2:21):** Sitting at the gate indicates an official position in the royal administration. This detail — seemingly minor — becomes the pivot for the entire narrative: Mordecai's position allows him to uncover the assassination plot, which in turn sets up the reversal that will save the Jewish people.

*— LOGOS*
